title: Segmented eval lanes with configurable privacy fences for Dedicated/Private customers
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a blueprint and implementation plan for 'segmented eval lanes' — customer-scoped evaluation pipelines that run on Dedicated and Private deployments with configurable privacy fences (no telemetry exports, hashing-only diffs, on-host golden sets). The feature should allow ops and platform engineers to tie regressions to config or model changes while guaranteeing customer data isolation and auditable privacy controls.
acceptance_criteria: Customers on Dedicated/Private can opt into a segmented eval lane per deployment via Console toggle or config file
Eval runs are executed inside customer-controlled environment (VPC/local host) or a logically isolated runner with no raw data export
Config/model change events trigger automatic snapshot evals and produce a regression report bound to that change id
Telemetry exported to Redwood for product analytics contains only hashed anchors and aggregated metrics unless customer explicitly enables telemetry export
Rollout gating supports: soft-warning, canary-block, and automatic rollback actions based on eval thresholds mapped to SLOs
tasks: Define API for per-deployment eval lane toggles and privacy profiles
Design on-host runner container spec and RBAC boundaries for Private deployments
Implement snapshot trigger on model/config change (Git tag + config hash)
Integrate delta-hash pipeline for local golden comparisons without leaking raw prompts
Console UX for enabling lanes, viewing regression diffs, and approving telemetry opt-in
Write e2e tests and compliance docs for SOC2 / data-sovereignty reviews
decisions: Default privacy profile will be 'hash-only' where all prompt/response anchors are salted and hashed before leaving customer boundary
We will support an explicit opt-in API for customers to allow Redwood to ingest plaintext eval artifacts for joint debugging
On Dedicated, we prefer runner-as-service inside customer's VPC over full-on-prem binaries for maintainability
Initial rollout will support prompt/response golden comparison and token-level metric aggregation; richer trace export will be post-beta

risks_mitigation: Risk: Customers may misconfigure telemetry opt-in causing accidental data leakage. Mitigation: Default to hash-only and require owner-confirmed consent for plaintext exports.
Risk: Runner incompatibilities with older on-prem infra. Mitigation: Provide both container runner and lightweight binary fallback; document kernel reqs.
Risk: Eval overhead increases latency for live traffic. Mitigation: Snapshot evals run asynchronously against stored traces or sampled requests; canary mode runs on mirrored traffic only.
